hypothesis: All 32 lanes in each wave read the same FP16 Q8 block scale, so loading/decoding it once in lane zero and broadcasting it might reduce redundant instructions without changing any weight value or FMA.

candidate.change: For each column and K iteration, lane zero decoded the FP16 block scale and __shfl-broadcast it; every lane retained its own int8 quant byte and original multiply/FMA order.
candidate.red: The candidate primitive fixture failed collection because its wave-scale wrapper and registry key did not exist.
candidate.green: The candidate registry key resolved and two primitive shapes were BF16-bit equal to exact pack8.

rocprof.command: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1100 HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/hipengine-hipcc-version-q3.txt HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 PYTHONPATH=. rocprofv3 --kernel-trace --output-format csv -d /tmp/hipengine-q8-wave-scale-reject-trace-20260720-152352 -o q8-wave-scale -- python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_gguf_q8_0_pack8_gemv_decode.py -k tile16x4-wave-scale
rocprof.conclusion: Resources match retained 16x4, so the regression is instruction latency: sixteen wave shuffles per K iteration cost far more than uniform cached scale loads/conversions.

decision.reason: Every production shape regressed by 38.77% to 191.80% despite exact outputs and zero scratch.
decision.cleanup: Removed the wave-scale template mode, HIP export, Python wrapper/registry key, and temporary tests; production sources are byte-identical to 2e2a97a3.
decision.next_action: Close dense-Q8 local schedule/codegen experiments at retained 16x4 and move to exact GDN, the next measured Amdahl family.
